constraint_decided_it: E19's scope note requires 'physical boundaries that separate them completely in an objective way from other objects' and says instances 'can be moved' -- whether an immobile building satisfies this is exactly what t0821 (msgs [9]-[12], Kritsotaki/Stead/Doerr, 2015) left unresolved, and the CRM's own building examples sit at plain E24 (Palace of Knossos, Colosseum, 'The building of Rome (E12) has produced the Colosseum (E24)' under P108; 'transformed the Venetian Loggia in Heraklion (E24)' under P124). A takes E24 and flags t0821 as unresolved; B asserts the E22 subclass with high confidence, sourcing it to t1170, which says 'new E19 object', and to E24's scope note, which says E24 -- neither says E22.
better_modelling: The officially adopted worked example for this exact pattern (P123/P124 examples, from Issue 404) dual-types the event: 'The transformation of the Venetian Loggia in Heraklion into a city hall (E81, E12) resulted in the City Hall of Heraklion (E24). [AND: has produced (P108) the City Hall of Heraklion]'. Neither answer types the 1938 re-erection as E12 Production, which E24's scope note presupposes ('describing the production process also as an instance of E81 Transformation') and which is what licenses calling the Combe Farm barn human-made. Full form: 1938 re-erection (E81, E12) P124 transformed Hollow Farm barn (E24), P123 resulted in / P108 has produced Combe Farm barn (E24); 1839 tithe survey (E31) P70 documents only the former. B's P92/P93 are the superproperties of P124/P123 and add nothing once those are asserted.
reasoning: Both reach the CRM-prescribed core -- two distinct E18 instances joined by one E81 Transformation via P124/P123 -- and both quote E24, E81, E11, E6 and E12 accurately; the E81 scope note's 'characteristic cases are reconstructions ... of historical buildings' plus Issue 404's requirement of substantial material change (new roof, new plinth, one bay rebuilt, not merely a change of use) settles E81 over E11 for both. A separates on two checkable points: it uses the class the CRM's own building examples use (E24), and it locates t0821, the thread that actually debates immobile buildings, quotes Doerr verbatim, and correctly reports that no SIG vote closed it. B substitutes t1170, a digression inside Issue 369 (Phase) about a rebuilt ship, and claims that thread 'was convened to test' the relocation position -- it was not, and it concerns repair/reconstruction, not relocation; B also attributes an 'E22 Human-Made Object' conclusion to sources that say E19 and E24. B's one real gain is the correct E31 -P70-> original barn link (P70 domain E31, range E1) that A leaves informal, which is why the margin is slight rather than clear.
